correctness.rationale: The digit-carry transition identity is derived directly from the number of 1^d occurrences. It partitions every integer change position into exact interior dyadic clusters and optional block-boundary changes, yielding all run lengths by gap enumeration. Congruence classes and convergent 2-adic valuation tails give exact rational densities for every length, with mass checks sum length*density=1. The standalone verifier checks all transitions and run gaps for d=2..8 to 2^18; this is supplemental finite evidence.

originality.rationale: A close primary theorem (Sobolewski, arXiv:2204.05287, Theorem 1.7) already implies the 2^d upper bound; this is explicitly credited. Its statement gives neither the exact set of attainable lengths nor the whole rational frequency law nor the transition-position classification. The directly relevant 2022 and 2024 block-additive correlation papers address different invariants. Searches of published-finding corpus, own accessible ledgers, and external literature did not identify a statement implying the new complete run spectrum and densities. Absolute unindexed coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The general upper bound L_max<=2^d is already in Sobolewski Theorem 1.7 and is not independently novel.
An unindexed paper or unpublished table could contain the all-rank distribution; database searches do not prove its absence.
The d=2 special case may be derivable by combining classical Rudin–Shapiro factor-frequency results, without implying this all-d classification.

value.rationale: The full all-d run-length spectrum and per-length rational density law is a natural complete classification of the monochromatic-run invariant of binary 1^d pattern-parity automatic words. It refines the known general maximum bound into exact positions, a sharp finite spectrum, and a full distribution including the non-random run-start density. The invariant is motivated independently by symbolic factor structure, autocorrelation heuristics, and run-length-limited behavior; it is not a parameter-tweaked textbook count. Residual bibliographic risk is disclosed.
